title: Video lecture (illustrative example)
subtitle: Shape example only. Segments and timestamps are placeholders for what a transcript pipeline would give you.

ui.why: Why the speaker says it matters
ui.learner: I watched a video and have its transcript. I do not know the subject.
ui.context: a single video lecture, studied from its transcript

prompts.explain: Using only the transcript segment I name, explain the idea in plain language. Define each term the first time. Tell me what the speaker skipped over, and mark anything that is your addition, not theirs.
prompts.evidence: Point to where in the video this is said (timestamp) and quote the one line. Then tell me whether an independent source agrees, and give the source.
prompts.challenge: Quiz me one question at a time on this segment. Hint before you answer. After five, tell me which timestamps to rewatch.
prompts.deeper: Go beyond the video: what is the standard objection, what has changed since it was recorded, and what should I read next.

controls.K2: Claim 2: the example that supports it

tree.s: What the speaker says, in the order they say it, with a way to check each part.

k.s: The speaker states what goes wrong today and why it matters.
k.w: Without this the rest has no point.

k.s: The core claim and its parts.
The one sentence the whole video builds toward.
A concrete case that the speaker uses to prove the thesis.

k.t: What the speaker did not prove
k.s: Gaps and assumptions to check outside the video.
k.w: A video is one voice. Verify before you rely on it.
